newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mercenary Denard to face Comoros trial in France.
newsitem.headline: Mercenary Denard to face Comoros trial in France.

text.p: Veteran French mercenary Bob Denard and two of his former lieutenants are to stand trial over the murder of Comoros President Ahmed Abdallah during a coup on the Indian Ocean archipelago, justice sources said on Tuesday.
They said an appeals court ruled that the 68-year-old Denard and soldiers of fortune Jean-Paul Guerrier and Dominique Malacrino must be tried in Paris' assize court over the 1989 assassination.
The three men appealed to the supreme court against the ruling, they said. No date was immediately set for the assize trial.
Denard, who had led the 1978 invasion that put Abdallah in power, is accused of complicity in his murder. Investigators believe the killing was carried out by Denard's men in the presidential guard.

Denard is also under investigation for his third raid in the Comoros late in 1995, when he and his 30 white mercenaries overthrew president Mohamed Said Djohar and were subsequently arrested by a French expeditionary force.
Denard was held in France for several months and released in July last year. He asserts that France approved of his interventions in Comoros.
The French troops did not return Djohar to power. Mohamed Taki is now president of the archipelago, with France's backing.
